drivingQuestion: Which part of the sciatic nerve does the Torah itself forbid?
outcomeNote: A single amoraic ruling with its prooftext; the challenge to it opens in the next unit.

segments.he: הָאוֹכֵל מִגִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה [וְכוּ׳]. אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא שֶׁעַל הַכַּף בִּלְבַד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עַל כַּף הַיָּרֵךְ״.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «One who eats» an olive-bulk «of the sciatic nerve» incurs forty lashes. «Shmuel says: The Torah prohibits only» the part of the sciatic nerve «that is on the» rounded protrusion of flesh shaped like «a spoon» that is near the end of the femur. This is «as it is stated» in the verse: “Therefore the children of Israel eat not the sciatic nerve that is «upon the spoon of the thigh”» (Genesis 32:33).
